title: A List of CEOs Is Not an Ownership Map

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: A list of CEOs is not an ownership map.
scenes.on_screen: A LIST OF NAMES ≠ OWNERSHIP MAP

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Picture a post showing media executives with one thing in common. Then it jumps to a claim about an entire community.
scenes.on_screen: THE JUMP FROM NAMES TO CONSPIRACY

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Hold on. Even a completely accurate list would not show who owns the shares, who has voting power, or who made a particular editorial decision.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: For a public company, start with official filings. Look for major shareholders, voting rights, and the board. Then investigate the decision you’re actually questioning.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Yes, a business can have conflicts of interest. Yes, powerful people deserve scrutiny. But being Jewish is not evidence of collusion with other Jewish people.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: An identity match isn’t a paper trail. A real investigation connects actions with evidence, not just names.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Investigate the company. Don’t turn a community into one.
scenes.on_screen: INVESTIGATE THE COMPANY · NOT A COMMUNITY
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
